title: Native nation or community profile
description: One Native nation, Alaska Native entity, Native Hawaiian community or Indigenous people of a U.S. territory: names, legal status, state presence, population, official contacts, government, justice institutions, published law, gaming, jurisdiction and consultation history. Stored as content/tribes/<first letter of id, or _other>/<id>.yaml. Every fact cites a source key and a confidence level; a field with no supporting source is left out.

imageReuse.description: Whether the project may show an image, and why. Reuse is assumed until a signal says otherwise (docs/official-images.md). The validator checks that status follows from the signals.

status.description: no-restriction-found: no signal limits reuse; the image may be shown with attribution and a way to ask for removal. conditions-apply: a signal allows reuse on conditions, given in its note; shown only where the conditions are met. needs-checking: a signal could not be read or confirmed; not shown until someone checks it. restricted: a signal limits reuse; not shown, the nation's page is linked instead. permission-granted: the nation gave permission (see permission); shown within its scope. permission-denied: the nation said no; not shown. withdrawn-at-request: the nation asked for removal; not shown, and the private copy is deleted.

checked.description: When the signals were last checked.

signals.description: Every signal found about reusing the image, including ones that do not restrict it.

kind.description: terms-of-use: the website's terms limit copying or display. copyright-notice: a general copyright line. trademark-notice: the site says its logos or seal are trademarks or otherwise protected. trademark-symbol: a trademark symbol (® or ™) is printed on the image. tribal-insignia-database: the nation filed this design in the USPTO Native American Tribal Insignia database. tribal-law: a law of the nation governs use of its seal, emblem, flag or logo. permission-required: the nation asks to be contacted before use. nation-request: the nation asked the project directly (decision record 0009).

quote.description: The words that carry the signal, copied exactly.

source.description: Source record for the page or law, when there is one.

serial_number.description: For a tribal-insignia-database signal: the entry's serial number.

date.description: For a nation-request signal: when the request arrived.

permission.description: The trail of any permission request to the nation.

entity_type.description: What kind of community the record describes. native-nation: a tribal nation, band, pueblo, rancheria, community or Alaska Native village, whatever its recognition. native-hawaiian: the Native Hawaiian community, which has no federally recognized governing entity and is never described with tribal status categories. territorial-indigenous-people: an Indigenous people of a U.S. territory (for example CHamoru, Refaluwasch or Samoan), whose status rests on territorial law. alaska-native-corporation: a corporation formed under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, which is not a government (reserved; not yet populated).

part_of.description: For a band or other component that the list of recognized entities names only inside another entity's entry (for example the six component reservations of the Minnesota Chippewa Tribe): the id of that entity's profile. The component's own recognition cites the same entry.

official.description: Name as it appears in the recognizing authority, or as the cited source gives it when there is none.

official_source.description: Source key for the official name.

self_designation.description: Names the nation uses for itself, including in its own language, exactly as the nation publishes them (never transliterated into ASCII).

romanized.description: A Latin-script form, only when the source gives one.

alternate.description: Other current names, including 'also known as' names in the federal list.

former.description: Earlier names, including 'previously listed as' names in the federal list.

pronunciation.description: How to say the nation's names, recorded only as an authoritative source publishes it: preferably the nation itself (its website, language program or a recording it published). Never worked out from the spelling. Left out when no such source is found.

name.description: The name being pronounced, written as the source writes it.

language_tag.description: Language of the name being pronounced, for example en for an English name or nv for a Diné Bizaad name.

respelling.description: A sound-it-out spelling, copied exactly as the source gives it, for example 'hoe-CHUNK'.

phonetic_transcription.description: A transcription in the International Phonetic Alphabet or another phonetic system, only when the source gives one, copied exactly.

recording.description: Link to an audio or video recording of the name that the source published.

recognition.description: Every legal status the community holds, each with its legal basis.

type.description: federal: on the Bureau of Indian Affairs list of recognized entities. state: recognized by a state. petitioning: has a pending petition for federal acknowledgment. unrecognized: no current recognition (for example a denied, withdrawn or inactive petition). congressional-special-relationship: Congress recognizes a special political and trust relationship with the people but no governing entity (Native Hawaiians). territorial-law: status rests on a territory's constitution or statutes.

state.description: For state or territorial status: which state or territory.

legal_basis.description: Citation of the law, regulation, notice or resolution that confers or describes the status.

petition_number.description: Federal acknowledgment petition number, as the Office of Federal Acknowledgment lists it.

petition_stage.description: Stage of the petition, worded as the source words it.

states.description: States and territories where the community has a presence. Drives the map; no boundaries are drawn.

census_areas.description: Census Bureau American Indian, Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian areas linked to the community. Census area codes are not identifiers of nations: one area can hold several nations, and nations without a land base have none, so each link is a matched fact with its own source and confidence.

geographic_identifier.description: Census GEOID of the area, for example the four-digit American Indian area code.

name.description: Area name as the Census Bureau gives it.

area_type.description: Census area type as given, for example reservation, off-reservation trust land, Oklahoma tribal statistical area or Alaska Native village statistical area.

vintage.description: Census vintage of the area definition.

population.description: Population or citizenship figures. Different kinds measure different things and are never added together.

kind.description: What the figure counts, from an open vocabulary (any lowercase hyphenated term). Suggested: citizens (the nation's own count of its citizens, or enrolled members where that is the nation's word), tribal-population-estimate, resident-population (everyone living in an area, Native or not), service-area-population, census-american-indian-alaska-native-alone, census-american-indian-alaska-native-alone-or-in-combination, census-native-hawaiian-alone, census-native-hawaiian-alone-or-in-any-combination, census-<group>-alone, census-<group>-alone-or-in-any-combination, other. Census kinds are self-identification, not citizenship.

contacts.description: Official, publicly published contact points of the government or office only. Never the names, personal email addresses or personal telephone numbers of officials or other people.

kind.description: contact-page is the nation's own Contact us page (a form, a staff or department list), recorded when it is on the nation's website; email-general is a general office address such as info@, never a person's own address.

label.description: Which office, for example 'Tribal government headquarters'.

link_status.description: For a website: lapsed when the address no longer belongs to the nation, for example a lapsed domain now showing unrelated content. The website shows a lapsed address as text, never as a link, and research scripts skip it.

official_images.description: The nation's seal, emblem, flag or logo. The nation's own website comes first; when it has none, another reliable copy may be used, such as a Wikimedia Commons file or the nation's page on an intertribal organization's website, with who made it and its license in credit. The record holds where the image was found and a fingerprint of the copy kept privately; the image file is never stored in this repository. Whether the project may show the image is recorded in reuse (docs/official-images.md). Never filled with an image the project drew or generated, or with a stock image.

kind.description: seal: the nation's official seal. emblem: an official crest or emblem the nation's law names as distinct from its seal. flag: the nation's flag. logo: the mark the nation uses on its website, which may include the seal.

alternative_text.description: The image's alternative text, exactly as the page gives it.

image_link.description: Where the image is served: the nation's website, or the other copy that credit names.

credit.description: Who made or published this copy, and its license, when it is not the nation's own file on the nation's own website; for example a Wikimedia Commons file drawn by a volunteer. Shown in the image's Sources entry.

media_type.description: As the server reported it, for example image/png.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file as downloaded, so a later copy can be checked against it.

private_copy.description: Path of the private copy under the project's private research captures (research/captures/ in the project files) and, once uploaded, under the same path in the private source documents bucket. Removing a nation's folder removes every copy.

tribal_insignia_database_entries.description: The nation's entries in the USPTO Native American Tribal Insignia database, which lists insignia a federally or state-recognized tribe has asked the Office to consider when it examines trademark applications. An entry is not a trademark registration and grants no rights; the Office does not check that the insignia is official.

serial_number.description: The entry's USPTO serial number (insignia entries use the 89 series).

wordmark.description: Words in the insignia, as the Office records them.

record_link.description: The entry's status page on the USPTO's Trademark Status and Document Retrieval system.

design_compared.description: How the filed design compares with the image in official_images, judged by eye.

private_copy.description: Path of the private copy of the Office's image of the insignia.

languages.description: Heritage languages, as the nation or an authoritative source names them.

federal_administration.description: The Bureau of Indian Affairs region and agency that serve the nation.

indian_health_service.description: The Indian Health Service Area that serves the nation and, where the Indian Health Service names them, its service units or health programs and who runs them. Each fact comes from one source; the Area is repeated in each so that a fact stands on its own.

area.description: Indian Health Service Area, such as Billings or Navajo.

service_unit.description: Service unit, service area or health program as the source names it.

operator.description: Who runs the nation's health services as the source states it: the Indian Health Service itself (Direct Service Tribes list), or the nation or a Tribal organization under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act.

government_structure.description: The legal form of the government, only where a source states it.

kind.description: indian-reorganization-act: constitution adopted under 25 U.S.C. § 5123. oklahoma-indian-welfare-act: under 25 U.S.C. § 5203. alaska-indian-reorganization-act: under the 1936 Alaska amendment, 25 U.S.C. § 5119. written-constitution-other: a written constitution adopted outside those Acts. traditional: a traditional form of government.

governance.description: How the nation's government is set up, one plain fact per item, as the nation's constitution or other governing document, its own website or an official directory states it: its governing body, head of government, elections, branches, courts and how its governing document is changed. Never a summary of a document; an aspect the sources do not state is left out, and the search for it is logged under research/search-logs/governance/ (decision record 0042).

aspect.description: Which part of the government the fact describes. form: the form of government or the authority the document is adopted under, in the source's words. governing-body: the name of the body holding lawmaking or governing power; -size, -selection and -term: its number of members, how they are chosen and their term. general-council: a body of all voting citizens and who sits in it. head-of-government: the title of the office that leads the government or presides over the governing body; -selection and -term likewise. other-officers: the titles of the other officers. elections: when regular elections are held. voting-age: the minimum age to vote. election-authority: the body that runs elections. branches: the branches the source names. separation-of-powers: the source states that the branches' powers are separate (value "Stated"). judiciary: the courts the source sets up or the power to set them up; judicial-selection and judicial-term: how judges are chosen and their term; judicial-independence: one protection the source gives judges or courts. amendment: how the governing document is changed. secretarial-approval: whether amendments or laws need the Secretary of the Interior's approval. recall-and-removal: how officials are removed or recalled.

value.description: The fact in a few plain words, with bodies and offices named as the source names them ("Business Committee", "Chairman") and numbers as digits ("7 members", "4 years").

quote.description: The words of the source that state the fact, copied exactly, reading errors of a scanned text included. Required when the fact comes from a document's text; scripts/governance/apply_answers.py checks that the quote is in the text before the fact is kept.

governing_documents.description: Where the nation's constitution, codes and court rules are published. Linked, not reproduced (see data-model.md on tribal legal texts).

kind.description: Open vocabulary (any lowercase hyphenated term). Suggested: judicial-branch (the nation's court system as a whole, such as a "Judicial Branch" or "Judiciary", not one court), tribal-court, court-of-appeals, supreme-court, intertribal-court, intertribal-court-of-appeals (a court several nations share, such as the Southwest Intertribal Court of Appeals), peacemaking-program, traditional-forum, healing-to-wellness-court, court-of-indian-offenses (a court operated under 25 C.F.R. Part 11, often called a CFR court), elders-council, other.

part_of.description: For one court of a group that sources also list as a whole, such as one of the Navajo Nation's district courts: the name of the group's entry in this profile's justice_institutions, written exactly as it is there. The nation page lists the court under its group, and the court shares the group's place on the path of appeal. The fact's own source must say the court belongs to the group.

location.description: Where the court sits, as its source gives it: the town or community, the state and, when the source gives one, the street address. Never filled in from the nation's own address or worked out from the court's name.

place.description: Town, community or chapter, as the source names it.

address.description: Street address, only when the source gives it.

appeals_to.description: Where appeals from this court go: the name of another court in this profile's justice_institutions, written exactly as it is there. It is its own cited fact, because the source that sets the path of appeal (a constitution, a court code, the court's own website) is often not the source that lists the court. Recorded only from a source that says so, never worked out from a court's name or kind. Left out for the highest court and when no source says.

dispute_resolution_law.description: Source keys of the nation's published laws on peacemaking, mediation, arbitration or related processes.

dispute_resolution.description: How the nation resolves disputes outside, alongside or within its courts, recorded only where a source documents it (never inferred from silence). Traditional or ceremonial details are recorded only as far as the nation itself has made them public (charter, commitment 5).

forums.description: Each dispute resolution forum or program the nation offers.

kind.description: Kind of method, from an open vocabulary: any lowercase hyphenated term is accepted, so methods not yet listed still validate. Use one of these where it fits: peacemaking, traditional-forum, mediation-program, arbitration, family-or-talking-circle, elders-council, restorative-justice, settlement-conference, family-group-conference, sentencing-circle, healing-circle, negotiation-assistance, ombudsperson, other. A kind that becomes common gets its own record (a method record in content/methods/ once that record type exists, or a glossary entry) rather than a schema change.

own_term.description: The nation's own name for the method, exactly as the nation writes it.

translation.description: An English rendering, only when the source gives one.

description.description: What the method is and how it works, in neutral words drawn from the source.

name.description: The forum's name as the nation gives it.

legal_basis.description: Code, constitution, court rule or resolution that sets up the forum, cited as the nation publishes it.

case_types.description: Kinds of matters the forum hears, from an open vocabulary (any lowercase hyphenated term). Suggested: family, child-welfare, juvenile, civil, criminal-diversion, criminal-sentencing, probate, property-or-land, housing, gaming, employment, commercial, elections, intergovernmental, other.

participation.description: How cases arrive, from an open vocabulary. Suggested: voluntary, court-referred, voluntary-or-court-referred, required, other.

relationship_to_court.description: How the forum relates to the Tribal court, in one or two neutral sentences from the source.

enforcement.description: How agreements or decisions are given effect, for example entered as a court order.

provisions.description: Specific published provisions on peacemaking, mediation, arbitration or traditional dispute resolution.

kind.description: Open vocabulary (any lowercase hyphenated term). Suggested: peacemaking, mediation, arbitration, traditional-dispute-resolution, other.

citation.description: Title, chapter and section as the nation publishes them.

summary.description: One neutral sentence, written only after reading the provision.

clauses.description: Dispute resolution terms in agreements and commercial law: arbitration or mediation clauses, choice of forum, and limited waivers of sovereign immunity.

context.description: Open vocabulary (any lowercase hyphenated term). Suggested: gaming-compact, commercial-code, secured-transactions-code, employment-code, intergovernmental-agreement, business-charter, other.

kind.description: Open vocabulary (any lowercase hyphenated term). Suggested: arbitration-clause, mediation-clause, meet-and-confer, choice-of-forum, waiver-of-sovereign-immunity, other.

training_programs.description: Programs that train or certify peacemakers, mediators or arbitrators for the nation's forums.

published_materials.description: Published rules, forms and guides for the nation's dispute resolution forums. Linked, not reproduced.

database_listings.description: Entries copied in bulk from a database or directory of tribal laws (such as the National Center on Restorative Justice Restorative Justice Tribal Laws Database) without opening the law itself. They are leads for review, not provisions: many concern diversion, treatment or sentencing rather than dispute resolution, and none is counted as a provision until it is read and moved to provisions (decision record 0015).

title.description: Title as the database gives it.

citation.description: Citation as the database gives it.

link.description: Link to the law as the database gives it.

practice_area.description: The database's practice area tags, as it writes them.

phase.description: The database's case phase tags, as it writes them.

form_of_practice.description: The database's form of practice tags, as it writes them.

gaming.description: Gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act (25 U.S.C. §§ 2701-2721).

status.description: The federal action on the compact. approved and deemed-approved follow 25 U.S.C. § 2710(d)(8); disapproved is a disapproval under § 2710(d)(8)(B); secretarial-procedures are Class III procedures issued by the Secretary of the Interior under § 2710(d)(7)(B)(vii) and 25 C.F.R. part 291 in place of a compact.

dispute_resolution_summary.description: One neutral sentence on how the compact resolves disputes between the nation and the state.

entities.description: The nation's gaming regulator and gaming enterprises.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdictional facts that shape how disputes reach tribal, state or federal forums.

value.description: Short value as defined for the topic in docs/data-model.md, for example mandatory-state, optional-state, not-a-public-law-280-state, excepted, retroceded, state-criminal-jurisdiction, exercising, implementing or designated-agent-listed.

jurisdiction_agreements.description: Agreements between the nation and a state, county, city or federal agency that share or allocate jurisdiction: cross-deputization and law-enforcement agreements, tax agreements and compacts other than gaming compacts, and child welfare agreements. One fact per agreement per source.

other_party.description: The state agency, county, city or federal agency that is party to the agreement, as the source names it.

agreement.description: The agreement's title, or a short description when it has none.

treaties.description: Ratified United States treaties signed by the nation or by the tribes and bands it descends from, each linked to its text in Kappler's Indian Affairs: Laws and Treaties. A link to a historic signatory is a matched fact with its own confidence.

title.description: The treaty's title as Kappler gives it.

statutes_at_large.description: Statutes at Large citation, such as 15 Stat. 667.

signatory.description: How the treaty names the party the nation descends from.

land_establishment.description: How the nation's reservation or other land base was set aside (treaty, executive order, statute, agreement, purchase or proclamation), with the instrument cited.

land_area.description: The reservation, rancheria, colony or other area as the source names it.

instrument.description: The treaty, order or act, in short citation form.

memberships.description: Intertribal organizations the nation belongs to, as the organization publishes its membership.

related_entities.description: Organizations related to the community that are not the community's government, for example an Alaska Native regional corporation or a state agency serving Native Hawaiians.

consultation.description: Dated history of this project's contact with the nation about the record, including corrections and redaction or withdrawal requests (charter, commitments 4 and 6). Name offices or roles, never individuals.

with.description: Office or role, for example 'Office of the Tribal Secretary'.

fields.description: Fields a correction or redaction concerns.

evidence_private.description: True when a copy of the correspondence is kept privately outside the repository.
